name: Matrei in Osttirol
kurzbeschreibung: The gateway to Nationalpark Hohe Tauern – your starting point for tours into the Venedigergruppe.
text:
Overview

Matrei in Osttirol serves as the economic and tourism hub of the Iseltal valley within the Lienz district of East Tyrol. This historic market town sits at an elevation of 975 metres in an expansive alpine basin where the rushing Tauernbach stream joins the glacial Isel river. Home to roughly 4,600 residents, Matrei is the second-largest municipality in Tyrol by land area and the bustling headquarters of the High Tauern National Park in East Tyrol. Encircled by more than 150 three-thousand-metre peaks belonging to the Venediger and Glockner mountain groups—including the glaciated Großvenediger (3,657 m)—Matrei blends centuries of heritage with world-class mountaineering and winter sports.

History

Human settlement in the basin traces back to prehistoric Illyrian and Celtic tribes, corroborated by substantial archaeological grave sites. The town first appeared in written records in 1170 as Matrei (historically Windisch-Matrei). A remarkable historical chapter was its six-century allegiance to the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg: from 1207 until secularization in 1803, the Matrei basin remained a Salzburgian enclave surrounded by the County of Tyrol, before formally joining Tyrol in 1814. The monumental parish church of Saint Alban, constructed in the late 18th century by Wolfgang Hagenauer with frescoes by Martin Knoller, stands as one of Tyrol's largest countryside basilicas. Schloss Weißenstein crowns a dolomite crag above town, while Saint Nicholas Church in Bichl preserves celebrated Romanesque frescoes from the 13th century.

Getting There

Matrei in Osttirol enjoys reliable year-round road connections. Traveling from the north via Salzburg or Munich, motorists follow the scenic Felbertauern Road (B108) through the Felbertauern Tunnel directly into the valley. From the south and Carinthia, drivers proceed along the B100 Drautal road to Lienz and head northward along the B108. Rail travelers take ÖBB services to Lienz main station, where frequent regional buses operated by the Tyrol Public Transport Network connect directly to Matrei's town center within half an hour.

Tips

A visit to the National Park House in Matrei is essential, presenting engaging multimedia exhibitions on the flora, fauna, and glaciers of the Hohe Tauern. In winter, the Großglockner Resort Kals-Matrei offers over 40 kilometres of panoramic slopes accessed directly from town via the modern Goldried gondola. In summer, explore the idyllic Gschlößtal valley—often lauded as the most beautiful head of valley in the Eastern Alps—where the Innergschlöß glacier trail leads past the historic Rock Chapel towards the sparkling ice tongues of the Schlatenkees glacier.
